findings.title: Non-ASCII separator passes validation but breaks idempotence
findings.detail: The validation rejects only ASCII letters and digits, but any non-ASCII separator is folded or dropped by `_to_ascii` on the next call, so the idempotence constraint (same options on both calls) fails. `slugify("a b", separator="é")` returns `"aéb"`, and `slugify("aéb", separator="é")` returns `"aeb"`; `slugify("a b", separator="·")` returns `"a·b"` and re-slugifying gives `"ab"`. The docstring's stated rationale ("such a separator cannot be told apart from word content") applies equally to these separators. The spec and plan chose the ASCII-only rule deliberately, so this is a judgment call rather than a blocker, but the only separators that actually survive a round trip are ASCII non-alphanumeric strings.
findings.evidence: src/textkit/slug.py:19 `if any(char.isascii() and char.isalnum() for char in separator):` combined with `_to_ascii` at line 14 `return decomposed.encode("ascii", "ignore").decode("ascii")`, which removes or folds every non-ASCII character before the separator run regex runs on the second call.

findings.title: Alphanumeric separator error prints top-level usage instead of slug usage
findings.detail: The `ValueError` from `slugify` is routed through the top-level `parser`, so `textkit slug --separator x Hello` prints `usage: textkit [-h] {slug,stats} ...` and `textkit: error: separator must not contain ...`, whereas the argparse-validated `--max-length abc` prints the slug subparser's usage (`usage: textkit slug [-h] [--separator SEPARATOR] [--max-length N] text`) and `textkit slug: error: ...`. The two usage errors for the same subcommand show different usage lines; the exit code and `usage:` substring are correct, so the tests pass, but the message is less helpful for the separator case.
findings.evidence: src/textkit/cli.py:66-67 `except ValueError as exc:` / `parser.error(str(exc))` where `parser` is the top-level parser built by `build_parser()`, not `slug_parser`.
